title: Godot vs unreal
author: bee_faced_shaman
selftext:
I’m looking for good resources on AI-assisted coding for Unreal Engine.



Over the past few months I’ve been using Godot with Claude Code, and the results were great.



It’s obvious that Godot works better with AI since everything is plain text, unlike Unreal.



The main reason I switched from Unreal to Godot was precisely that using Godot with AI is easier. In the meantime, an MCP for Unreal came out that I wanted to test.



Unfortunately, from what I’ve observed, the results are much worse. I’ve since learned that Unreal requires more setup (the toolkit needs to be installed).



Has anyone had experience using AI with both Unreal and Godot? I’m looking for tips and suggestions — maybe someone would be willing to share their markdown file.

comments.author: FutureLynx_
comments.body:
I made many posts saying that Unreal had to drop blueprint system. Even before AI i was a critic of Blueprints, even though i see its benefits and learned a lot of it.

I said that if Unreal wants to survive it needs to ditch blueprints. I knew at the time that this was edgy and would trigger people, and that unreal could never drop blueprints.

These posts were downvoted. My comments were downvoted and with a lot of answers that didnt even make sense that were upvoted. And I had to remove these posts.

Recently Epic announce they are scrapping blueprints entirely.

I think this is great news, and maybe Unreal will have a second wind. I was preparing to leave for godot.

But at the moment I want to see what will come of it.

Blueprints was never good, even in the times without AI. The fact people defended it fanatically is crazy.

Blueprints are bad for performance, are bad for maintainability. Are a slow workflow. It splits your logic into 2 places.

Blueprints only benefit was tricking people into thinking they could make a game without learning how to code.

replies.author: hugot4eboss
replies.body:
Pretty much any tool that lets you connect it to vs code / jetrider or other ide, has like 90% code ready to be used as MCP, just need small adjustments.

Godot doesn't have official MCP and no 1 mainstream community made one either.

Spend like a day or two on creating your own via some LLM. Might get a MCP personalized just for your game not just for Godot

replies.author: tabaxi_gf
replies.body:
There is no need to make a MCP for Godot because Claude can just directly create the data files because they are just text as OP mentions. 

The editor also can notice that things have changed on disk so you can be running the editor and have Claude be modifying Godot assets at the same time. It will just pop a reload dialog.

replies.author: bee_faced_shaman
replies.body: I don't use mcp at all

comments.author: _playlogic_
comments.body:
As someone who has built custom MCP frameworks for both platforms; Unreal issues is that there currently is no external way to for the AI to drive all systems. First most systems are built as plugins making it hard for things like remote control, python, or even a custom  CPP plugins that give access to the engine. Blueprint  are going away but not nodal system entirely.  What people don’t understand is that Unreal Engine has been a closed system for decades, with 6 they are trying to change that. Also if you are an old hat like me, you will know this is not the first scripting language Epic has tried to implement. 

As far as Godot and MCPs; I won’t beat this drum…but when things get complex, you are going to find out quickly that  having an Agent only working directly on files and with the Godot CLI is going end painfully. 

If you want my honest take; if you want better graphic fidelity then Godot, look at Unity… I doubt you will hit any fee given the current state of the industry. But with that said, know that your the art production work is going to increase x4 over. If still set on Unreal and you plan on using fab for assets, know that Unreal is a beast built for massive teams. You are going to spend time learning features and optimizing then building your game. 

My advice, build something small in Godot, focus on game play loop and finish it end to end and release it on itch.io before trying to work on your dream game in unreal
